title: Traveling by Car
conversation: Sara and Nick are taking a car trip. Nick has taken a wrong turn, and now they need to stop and ask for directions. Sara: Do you think we can make it to Joe and Mary's by 7? Nick: I hope so. It's only 5 o'clock now and we've only got about 120 miles to go. We're making good time. Sara: Yes, but we still need to make a pit stop. Don't you want to stop somewhere and grab a bite? Nick: I guess so. Let's look for a place we can turn off. Sara: I just saw a sign that said Route 584 North. Aren't we supposed to be on 80 East! Nick: Yes. We must've taken a wrong turn somewhere. Sara: I thought you said you knew the roads like the back of your hand. Did you doze off or what? Nick: We'd better stop at a gas station and ask for directions. (at a gas station) Sara: Hi. We're lost. Can you tell me the quickest way to get on 80 East? Clerk: Hang a left out of the gas station. Hop on 35 South. Take it about 10 miles and you'll see a sign for 80 East. Sara: Thanks a lot. (back in the car) Nick: Did you get the directions? Sara: Yes. Left out of here, then 35 South to 80 East. Nick: Got it. Sara: Careful! You almost hit a piece of tire in the road. Nick: Please don't be a backseat driver! Sara: I try to bite my tongue, but sometimes I can't help myself.

idioms.meaning_en: to travel quickly or faster than expected
idioms.meaning_vi: đi nhanh, di chuyển thuận lợi và đúng tiến độ
idioms.example: There was no traffic, so we made good time on our drive to the coast.

idioms.meaning_en: to make a brief stop during a journey for fuel, food, or to use the restroom
idioms.meaning_vi: dừng xe tạm thời để đổ xăng, ăn nhẹ hoặc đi vệ sinh
idioms.example: Let's make a pit stop at the next rest area.
idioms.context: Yes, but we still need to make a pit stop.

idioms.meaning_en: to get something quick to eat
idioms.meaning_vi: ăn nhanh một bữa lót dạ
idioms.example: Do you want to grab a bite before the movie starts?
idioms.context: Don't you want to stop somewhere and grab a bite?

idioms.meaning_en: to leave a road to enter an exit or another road
idioms.meaning_vi: rẽ khỏi đường chính, chuyển hướng đi vào đường khác
idioms.example: You need to turn off at junction 15 to get to the hotel.
idioms.context: Let's look for a place we can turn off.

idioms.meaning_en: to turn onto the wrong road; to go in the wrong direction
idioms.meaning_vi: rẽ nhầm đường, đi sai hướng
idioms.example: I think we took a wrong turn at the roundabout.
idioms.context: We must've taken a wrong turn somewhere.

idioms.idiom: like the back of one's hand
idioms.example: She has lived here all her life and knows the town like the back of her hand.
idioms.context: I thought you said you knew the roads like the back of your hand.

idioms.meaning_en: to fall into a light sleep unintentionally
idioms.example: He was so tired that he began to doze off during the presentation.
idioms.context: Did you doze off or what?

idioms.example: Drive straight ahead and hang a left at the post office.
idioms.context: Hang a left out of the gas station.

idioms.meaning_en: to enter or get onto a highway, road, or vehicle quickly
idioms.meaning_vi: nhập làn, đi vào một con đường hay tuyến cao tốc
idioms.example: Hop on Interstate 95 and take exit 24.
Once you explain the rule, I'm sure everyone will get it.

idioms.meaning_en: a passenger who gives unwanted driving advice to the driver; someone who meddles without being in control
idioms.meaning_vi: người ngồi sau chỉ tay năm ngón, hay can thiệp vào cách lái xe của người khác
idioms.example: Stop telling me to brake; you're being such a backseat driver!
idioms.context: Please don't be a backseat driver!

idioms.meaning_en: to stop oneself from speaking or saying something that might cause trouble
idioms.meaning_vi: kiềm chế lời nói, bấm bụng nhịn nói
idioms.example: I wanted to disagree with him, but I decided to bite my tongue.
idioms.context: I try to bite my tongue, but sometimes I can't help myself.

idioms.meaning_en: to be unable to prevent or restrain oneself from doing something
idioms.meaning_vi: không thể kìm nén, không cưỡng lại được
idioms.example: The joke was so funny that she couldn't help herself and burst out laughing.
idioms.context: I try to bite my tongue, but sometimes I can't help myself.
